## Proof

We determine the cardinality of the set $\Pi(\mathbb{N})$ of all partitions of $\mathbb{N}$.

**Upper bound: $|\Pi(\mathbb{N})| \le 2^{\aleph_0}$.**

A partition of $\mathbb{N}$ is a collection of nonempty, pairwise disjoint subsets whose union is $\mathbb{N}$. Every partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathbb{N}$ induces an equivalence relation $\sim_{\mathcal{P}}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, where $m \sim_{\mathcal{P}} n$ iff $m$ and $n$ lie in the same block. Conversely, every equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}$ determines a unique partition (its equivalence classes). Thus partitions of $\mathbb{N}$ are in bijection with equivalence relations on $\mathbb{N}$.

An equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}$ is a subset of $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, i.e., an element of $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$. Since $|\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}| = \aleph_0$, we have $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})| = 2^{\aleph_0}$. The set of equivalence relations is a subset of $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})$, so

$$|\Pi(\mathbb{N})| \le 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

**Lower bound: $|\Pi(\mathbb{N})| \ge 2^{\aleph_0}$.**

Consider partitions of $\mathbb{N}$ into exactly two blocks. For each subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $A \neq \emptyset$ and $A \neq \mathbb{N}$, the pair $\{A,\, \mathbb{N}\setminus A\}$ is a partition of $\mathbb{N}$ into two blocks. Two such subsets $A$ and $B$ yield the same two-block partition iff $B = A$ or $B = \mathbb{N}\setminus A$.

The number of nonempty proper subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ is $2^{\aleph_0} - 2 = 2^{\aleph_0}$ (subtracting the two cases $A=\emptyset$ and $A=\mathbb{N}$, which does not change the infinite cardinality). Each partition $\{A, \mathbb{N}\setminus A\}$ is counted exactly twice (once by $A$, once by $\mathbb{N}\setminus A$), so the number of distinct two-block partitions is

$$\frac{2^{\aleph_0}}{2} = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

Since the two-block partitions are a subset of all partitions,

$$|\Pi(\mathbb{N})| \ge 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

**Conclusion.**

Combining both bounds,

$$|\Pi(\mathbb{N})| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The cardinality of the set of all partitions of $\mathbb{N}$ equals $2^{\aleph_0}$, the cardinality of the continuum.
